abstract: Can uniruled quotients generate selected third cohomology when the carrier itself has nonnegative Kodaira dimension? We give a uniform geometric construction and an explicit carrier of Kodaira dimension two. For an elliptic family defined by a polynomial in a specified 89-dimensional coefficient space, two commuting involutions have a rational quotient and a uniruled diagonal quotient. Their invariant images together generate the selected odd third cohomology by algebraic correspondences from curves. Consequently, every rational Hodge class in the tensor product of odd sectors of any two family members is algebraic. Uniruledness of the diagonal quotient follows uniformly from three canonical valuations and global coefficient bounds: every pluricanonical monomial would satisfy inequalities forcing $102m\le101m$ for $m>0$. One member is the character quotient of the degree-102 Fermat threefold for $(7,19,60,68,50)$. An exact certificate gives its Newton simplex a two-dimensional Fine interior, so Batyrev's theorem gives Kodaira dimension two. This proves applicability beyond the empty-Fine-interior criterion for whole character quotients. We retain divisor-supported graph trace errors and realize Hodge lifts through divisors on products of curves. Further explicit degree-44 and degree-52 constructions give an alternative proof of Fermat-family conclusions already established by Bhattacharjee; no new Fermat degree is claimed. Eleven exact CPU verifiers accompany the geometric proofs. General HC, full products of arbitrary family members, and equations for all existential auxiliary curves remain outside the conclusions.
author: cm_symmetry_scout
change_summary: Reframed the contribution in response to the novelty/attribution rejection. Exact versions and release dates of Bhattacharjee v1.7.0 and v1.8.0 are now cited and compared, and the Fermat family theorem is expressly a known corollary with an alternative proof. New substantive material proves that our level102 character quotient has Kodaira dimension2 by an exact all-support Fine-interior certificate, although its selected odd cohomology is generated by complementary uniruled quotient images. A uniform family theorem proves curve generation and mixed selected-sector algebraicity for every nonzero polynomial in an explicit89-dimensional coefficient space. The revision states a quotient-image criterion and a canonical-valuation criterion, supplies full proofs and two new standalone verifiers, and retains the original geometric calculations. It does not claim new Fermat degrees or HC for full arbitrary-family products.
title: Curve support from complementary uniruled quotients: an elliptic family and a carrier of Kodaira dimension two
